lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: Quiet doesn't mean idle in Toronto; it means the ledger is being rewritten in pencil, and the first line reads Darren Raddysh's arrival, plus the buzz around Alexander Bilecki, has given this offseason some backbone. The Leafs are in the deep offseason now, with no games to sell and no excuses left to hide behind - only construction. Last year is gone, and the record is just a memory; what matters is whether these additions actually harden the blue line and deepen the roster. Raddysh looks like the kind of sensible pickup a contender makes when it's tired of patchwork, while Bilecki's prospect surge gives the front office a younger, cheaper piece to dream on. Training camp is next, and it will tell us whether this remade roster is merely busier - or genuinely better.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The Blue Jays' winter is already doing what every hard offseason does - exposing the weak seams and daring the club to stitch them fast. Brandon Barriera and Jake Bloss head the Arizona Fall League group, a sharp sign Toronto is still hunting for arms with upside while the roster waits for clarity. The club sits at 73-74, fourth in the division, and that middling finish makes every decision feel heavier, not lighter. Bo Bichette's free agency looms like the headline no one can dodge, and the rotation still needs answers after all the elbow smoke and shoulder alarms. The Jays can't afford pretty talk now. Watch the Fall League arms, and watch whether Toronto turns that uncertainty into a move before camp opens.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The offseason has a pulse again - and it starts with Kawhi Leonard, the long-delayed swing that could change Toronto's whole autumn. The Raptors are expected to move forward on the Leonard deal after the league cleared the way and the suspension threat vanished, a deal that's been parked in neutral since July while the franchise covered its bet. Toronto enters September with no games on the board and no room for drift; the next six weeks are about turning paperwork into a roster and a plan. Leonard, Brandon Ingram and the rest of that reshaped core are the story now, not last spring's residue. It's a serious bet for a team that wants to matter again. What to watch next: the formal completion of the trade and the Sept. 29 camp opening, when the new pecking order finally gets tested.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The quiet before a season opener can fool a team, but Washington has plenty humming under the hood. Tress Way said this 2026 season will likely be his last - a poignant note for a franchise still leaning on its longest-tenured voice and one of the league's steadiest legs. The Commanders' offseason has given way to the hard edge of September, with Daron Payne listed as limited and the line already drawing concern before the first snap. There's no hiding the roster's fault lines now. Washington finished 0-0 in the offseason, and the real work is here: keeping Jayden Daniels upright, sorting the trench health, and measuring how much loss the club can absorb in the kicking game when Way eventually walks away. What matters next is the Eagles opener and the first true test of this rebuilt spine.

paragraphs: The Leafs are deep into a noisy offseason, with Sportsnet weighing whether the roster is actually better and where the biggest questions still sit. Darren Raddysh also has a new chapter, reflecting on the path that led him to Toronto. The Blue Jays are staring at a rotation dilemma as they push toward the postseason, with a pivotal series against Baltimore looming in current coverage.

For the Raptors, the offseason stays quiet on the court, though team coverage is still spinning around familiar names like Chris Paul. The Commanders turn to Week 1 prep against Philadelphia, and one recent note flagged Deebo Samuel as a troubling glimpse of what Washington let go.
